entry.title: Files pass validation… then break in production
entry.summary:
Most upload pipelines check file type and size — and assume the file is safe. But that’s exactly where things go wrong. Real issues often show up later — when files are actually used. malware hidden in uploads exposed API keys in config files payloads that look valid but break at runtime The problem isn’t validation. It’s when validation happens. Files are trusted too early. By the time something breaks, it’s already in production. I built a Strapi plugin that scans files right after upload, before they’re ever used. Upload → Scan → Verdict
Right after upload — before anything touches production. Instead of trusting files based on format, it checks what’s actually inside. It catches malware, exposed secrets, and unsafe payloads — including issues that pass validation but fail later at runtime. GitHub: https://github.com/cyphernetsecurity/cypherscan-strapi
npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/strapi-plugin-cypherscan
Demo: https://youtu.be/zRk-9Es7mwA How are you handling file validation today? At upload — or only when things break?

entry.title: Can your AI model smell bullsh1t? BullshitBench has the receipts.
entry.summary: A new benchmark is asking a deceptively simple question: when you give an AI a nonsense prompt, does it call you out — or does it just roll with it? A 3-judge panel (Claude + GPT + Gemini) then scores each response: Clear Pushback = the model rejects the broken premise outright. Partial Challenge = it flags issues but still engages.
